requirement: These rules apply to the _parts KiCad footprint library, including the dot_matrix R2 footprint cohort. The part datasheet and symbol pin mapping always govern.

Orient the KiCad footprint horizontally when the governing datasheet package or recommended-land-pattern drawing shows the part horizontally. Orient it vertically when that drawing shows the part vertically.

Apply the selected orientation consistently to the pads, F.Silkscreen, F.Fab, F.Courtyard, reference and value text, and 3D model. If the datasheet provides no clear governing orientation, mark compliant_y_n No and explain the ambiguity and rationale in evidence_or_notes rather than choosing an orientation arbitrarily.

F.Cu must contain every copper land shown in the governing manufacturer-recommended PCB land pattern. Do not interpret package terminals, stencil openings, thermal vias, or solder-mask features shown in other diagrams as additional copper lands.
Use the recommended land-pattern center as footprint origin (0,0) unless the datasheet specifies another datum. Locate every pad by its center according to the datasheet dimensions.

Number pads according to the datasheet electrical terminal mapping and the corresponding symbol: Physically separated copper lands may share a pad number when they represent the same electrical terminal. Assign an exposed pad the datasheet-designated terminal number or the number required by the verified symbol mapping. Use unnumbered pads only for non-electrical mechanical metal features that are intended to be soldered. A footprint shall not assign a net merely because a support, locator, shell, fastener, or other inserted feature is metal. Any intentional electrical bond must be numbered, represented in the symbol, and connected visibly through the schematic.

If the datasheet does not provide a recommended land pattern, do not treat the package-terminal drawing as one. Obtain a manufacturer mechanical drawing or an approved documented derivation before treating the footprint as complete.

Use the pad shape shown by the governing land pattern: Use a rectangle when the datasheet shows explicit sharp rectangular corners. Use a rounded rectangle when the datasheet shows rounded rectangular corners, using the specified corner radius. When the corner geometry is unspecified, use a rounded rectangle with a 0.05 mm corner radius.
If a 0.05 mm corner radius is geometrically impossible because the pad is too narrow, flag the footprint for manual review rather than silently changing the radius.
Use a custom pad only when the datasheet copper geometry cannot be represented accurately by a rectangle or rounded rectangle. Shape and size the custom pad according to the governing land pattern.

All other pad requirements still apply to custom pads, including center location, numbering, copper clearance, solder-mask behavior, solder-paste behavior, and orientation. Do not use a custom pad as a workaround for geometry that a standard pad can represent accurately.

Prefer apertures derived automatically from the copper pad when the F.Mask or F.Paste aperture: Has the same size and shape as the copper pad, or Differs by a uniform change that can be represented accurately by the applicable solder-mask expansion, solder-paste absolute clearance, or solder-paste ratio in the pad clearance overrides and settings.

Include F.Mask and F.Paste in the copper pad's layer set when using automatic derivation. Enter mask and paste adjustments only in their corresponding settings; do not place these values in electrical pad clearance.

When a mask or paste aperture does not match the copper geometry and cannot be derived accurately from it: Remove the affected F.Mask or F.Paste layer from the underlying copper pad as necessary. Create separate unnumbered SMD Aperture objects on the appropriate F.Mask or F.Paste layer. Shape, size, and locate every separate aperture according to the datasheet. Use separate apertures for segmented exposed-pad stencil windows and other nonuniform paste patterns.

Pads should normally have 0 degrees rotation. The horizontal dimension as drawn is the KiCad pad width, and the vertical dimension as drawn is the KiCad pad height. A vertically elongated pad remains unrotated with a larger height than width.
Rotate a pad only when the governing land pattern actually specifies an angled or radial land. The overall footprint orientation rule does not justify rotating individual pads.
These rules govern every footprint containing one or more drilled features. They supplement the general copper-pad rules above and take precedence where an SMD-only rule is not applicable.

The manufacturing baseline is JLCPCB rigid FR-4 service as verified on 2026-08-26. The governing references are JLCPCB's PCB capabilities (https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/Capabilities), via and pad-hole tolerance explanation (https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/difference-and-tolerance-explanation-between-via-and-pad-holes), via-covering guide (https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/pcb-via-covering), and NPTH design guide (https://jlcpcb.com/blog/npth-design-guide). Recheck these sources before relying on the limits for a fabrication release because manufacturing capabilities can change.

Use the following conservative project limits unless a project-specific fabrication profile is stricter: Circular drilled holes: JLCPCB lists 0.15 mm through 6.30 mm; holes larger than 6.30 mm are CNC-routed. Controlled plated component-hole tolerance: +0.13 / -0.08 mm from the nominal finished-hole diameter. Preferred minimum plated component hole: 0.50 mm. PTH annular ring for ordinary 1 oz rigid boards: use at least 0.25 mm radially. JLCPCB lists smaller absolute limits, but those limits are not library defaults. Preferred ordinary via hole: at least 0.20 mm. Do not use JLCPCB's extreme minimum via geometry as a library default. Minimum NPTH diameter: 0.50 mm. Minimum plated-slot width: 0.50 mm on a 2-layer board and 0.35 mm on a multilayer board. Use 0.50 mm as the library-wide default minimum. Minimum non-plated-slot width: 1.00 mm. Minimum drilled-edge clearance between ordinary pad holes: 0.45 mm. Minimum drilled-edge clearance between vias: 0.20 mm. Copper clearance from an NPTH or non-plated slot edge: use at least 0.25 mm; increase it for screw heads, washers, conductive hardware, board-edge stress, or a stricter source.

Meeting a published minimum does not make a geometry preferred. A source-backed footprint should use robust normal-process dimensions and must not depend on an extra-cost or extreme process unless that exception is explicitly documented.
Treat the KiCad drill value and the fabrication drill output as the nominal finished hole. Do not add a separate allowance for plating after selecting that value.

Determine the maximum lead envelope from the governing component drawing: Round lead: use the maximum lead diameter. Square lead: use the diagonal of the maximum square, not one side. Rectangular lead: use the diagonal of the maximum rectangular cross-section unless the manufacturer specifies an oriented plated slot. Flat blade or tab: use the manufacturer-specified plated-slot dimensions and orientation. Tolerance: use the source maximum dimensions, including explicit lead tolerance, plating, burr, or deformation allowance when stated.

For an ordinary hand- or machine-inserted lead, choose a nominal finished hole at least 0.20 mm larger in diameter than the maximum lead envelope, then round upward to the next 0.10 mm drill size. JLCPCB's 0.10 mm lead-to-hole difference is the absolute project minimum and may be used only when a source or assembly constraint requires it and the footprint checklist documents the exception.

Use a larger insertion allowance when the part drawing, lead finish, manual-assembly method, pin count, or alignment tolerance requires it. Never reduce the hole below the datasheet-specified hole. Press-fit and compliant-pin holes are exceptions: use the connector manufacturer's finished-hole and plating specification exactly, select JLCPCB's controlled press-fit process, and identify the holes in the fabrication notes. Do not derive press-fit geometry from these ordinary soldered-lead rules.
If a datasheet omits the maximum lead envelope or the required finished hole, the footprint is incomplete until a manufacturer drawing or approved mechanical source supplies it.

Use annular-ring width, not a ratio alone, as the primary manufacturing constraint. For a circular hole of diameter H, the default circular pad diameter is: pad diameter = round up to 0.10 mm(max(H + 0.50 mm, 1.50 x H)) This provides at least a 0.25 mm radial annular ring and at least a 1.50:1 pad-to-hole ratio. For an oval plated slot, apply the same rule independently to the slot width and slot length. A manufacturer land pattern may require a larger pad and always governs when it does.

Use this reduced standard set when the source permits it: | documented standard | Nominal finished hole | Default minimum pad size | | pth_0.60_1.10 | 0.60 mm | 1.10 mm | | pth_0.80_1.30 | 0.80 mm | 1.30 mm | | pth_1.00_1.50 | 1.00 mm | 1.50 mm | | pth_1.20_1.80 | 1.20 mm | 1.80 mm | | pth_1.50_2.30 | 1.50 mm | 2.30 mm | | pth_2.00_3.00 | 2.00 mm | 3.00 mm | | pth_2.50_3.80 | 2.50 mm | 3.80 mm | | pth_3.00_4.50 | 3.00 mm | 4.50 mm |

Do not round downward to reach one of these configurations. If the required hole falls between rows, calculate and round the hole and pad upward. A smaller annular ring requires a documented source constraint, a JLCPCB capability check, and an explicit footprint-checklist exception. The exception must declare the reduced acceptance threshold. The saved pad must still meet that declared threshold; an exception does not disable geometry validation.

Use source_defined when the governing drawing specifies a finished hole or plated slot outside this table. The checklist may treat the listed or calculated pad size as a minimum when the source does not specify copper-land dimensions; larger copper is permitted only when it preserves all other required clearances. Use an exact-size policy when the manufacturer specifies the copper land.

Configure every ordinary soldered component lead as follows: Pad type: Through-hole (thru_hole). Pad number: exact datasheet and symbol terminal number. Hole shape and dimensions: round or oval exactly as derived from the source. Copper layers: all copper layers (*.Cu) unless a reviewed high-density design deliberately removes unused inner-layer annuli. Technical layers: *.Mask; do not include F.Paste or B.Paste. Pad clearance: leave blank so KiCad 9 inherits board and netclass rules. In KiCad 9, a literal 0 means zero clearance and is not the same as blank. Solder-mask expansion: leave blank/inherited unless the manufacturer drawing or fabrication profile specifies an override. Paste absolute and relative clearances: blank, with no paste layers. Zone connection, thermal relief gap, spoke width, and teardrops: inherit from the parent footprint, zone, or board rules unless a source-backed electrical or thermal requirement justifies an override. Hole-to-pad offset: zero unless the manufacturer drawing specifies an offset land. Fabrication property: None for an ordinary component lead; use Mechanical, Heatsink, or Castellated only when its KiCad meaning and the physical feature both apply.

When the land drawing does not specify pad shape: Pad 1: rectangular, to provide a conventional THT pin-one indication. Other round-hole electrical pads: circular. Oval plated slots: oval pad aligned to the slot. Solderable mechanical tabs: the source-defined shape; use an unnumbered plated pad unless the tab is an electrical terminal. Custom pad: permitted only when a standard shape cannot reproduce the source land. The checklist must include the complete custom geometry.
A source-defined shape overrides these defaults. Vias do not have pin numbers or a pin-one shape; the pad-one distinction applies only to component THT pads.

The pad-one shape supplements, but does not replace, the required F.Silkscreen and F.Fab pin-one or polarity indication. A connector keying-side indicator also does not replace the pin-one indication; the two marks communicate independent mechanical and electrical orientation information.

For a connector with a rectangular projected body, establish one source-backed body rectangle. Use that rectangle as the F.Fab body outline. Derive the F.Silkscreen body projection from the same rectangle, changing only line width and source-required copper clipping. Derive F.Courtyard from the union of that same body rectangle, all protruding physical features, and all copper pads, followed by the normal exact 0.25 mm courtyard offset. Do not use unrelated body extents, centers, or dimensions on the three layers.

When the manufacturer documents a latch, lock, keyed slot, shroud opening, tongue, or other feature that mechanically polarizes a rectangular connector, place the standardized keying-side indicator defined by FP-CONN-003 on both F.Fab and F.Silkscreen. Center the indicator on the outside edge corresponding to the documented feature. The indicator communicates only which side is mechanically polarized; it does not replace the source-accurate projected body outline or the required pin-one indication. Do not add it to an unpolarized connector.

Draft the keying-side indicator as a separate three-segment U-shaped bracket 1.00 mm wide and 0.50 mm deep. Place it outside the projected body with its open side facing the body. Center it along the applicable body edge and place the two open tips exactly 0.25 mm from that edge. Use 0.05 mm line width on F.Fab and 0.15 mm on F.Silkscreen. Apply the normal exact silkscreen-to-copper clearance if clipping is required. The indicator is an annotation and does not affect F.Courtyard. Do not reproduce internal connector construction, contact cavities, latch details, or decorative geometry on F.Silkscreen.

Actual vias are board objects, not footprint pads. A footprint may contain only the F.Fab documentation markers defined under Manufacturer-required via markers on F.Fab. Place and electrically verify the physical vias in PCB Editor.

Use these standard through-via configurations to minimize drill classes: | Use | Finished hole | Via diameter | Radial annular ring | | Dense, specifically approved | 0.20 mm | 0.50 mm | 0.15 mm | | Default signal and thermal | 0.30 mm | 0.60 mm | 0.15 mm | | Robust, power, or repeated thermal cycling | 0.40 mm | 0.80 mm | 0.20 mm |

Configure the KiCad via fields as follows unless the board's fabrication profile says otherwise: Via type: Through. Layer top/bottom: F.Cu to B.Cu. Padstack mode: Normal with the same diameter on all copper layers. Annular rings: all copper layers. Net: the actual connected net. A thermal via in an exposed pad normally uses that exposed-pad net; never leave a physical via on an arbitrary net merely because an F.Fab guide was unconnected. Front and back tenting: From design rules by default. If explicitly set, tent both sides unless a reviewed assembly or thermal requirement needs an opening. Covering, plugging, filling, and capping: off/default for normal service. Via-in-pad, filled, capped, or copper-filled construction requires an explicit JLCPCB order option, source-backed geometry, and fabrication review. Teardrops: inherit the board rule; they do not change the documented drill or annulus. Locked: optional placement protection only; it has no manufacturing meaning. Backdrill, post-machining, blind, buried, or microvia fields: off. Any use requires a project-specific fabrication profile and explicit manufacturer confirmation.

For ordinary solder-mask tenting, prefer via holes no larger than 0.40 mm; JLCPCB does not guarantee full tenting for larger holes. An intentionally exposed via must maintain at least 0.20 mm clearance from other exposed copper for HASL, or use a reviewed surface-finish/process exception.

Manufacturer-required via diameter, hole, pitch, and array geometry override the standard table only after they are checked against the selected fabrication process. The footprint checklist must distinguish a required array from a merely illustrative example layout.

Classify every non-signal drilled feature by its intended assembly and electrical function, not merely by the material passing through it: Plastic locating or alignment pin: unnumbered NPTH, Mechanical pad. Nonconductive support post: unnumbered NPTH, Mechanical pad. Metal locating pin, support, or other feature that merely passes through the PCB and is not intended to be soldered or electrically contacted: unnumbered NPTH, Mechanical pad with the required copper clearance. Metal support leg or tab intended to be soldered but having no electrical function: unnumbered plated Through-hole pad with *.Cu and *.Mask. It remains electrically unconnected. Metal shell, support, or mounting feature that the source and system design explicitly define as an electrical terminal or bond: numbered plated Through-hole pad matching a symbol pin. Connect it through the schematic to the intended GND, CHASSIS, or SHIELD net; do not assume signal ground. Manufacturer-specified non-plated slot: unnumbered NPTH oval hole or routed mechanical outline, exactly as the source requires.

"Purely mechanical" and "intentionally bonded" are mutually exclusive classifications. Once a feature is assigned an electrical net, it is an electrical terminal even when its primary purpose is structural. Solderable metal must retain a plated land, while unsoldered locating hardware, plastic features, and intentionally isolated hardware must not acquire copper plating. Never assign GND solely because the inserted feature is metal.

Ordinary screw and mounting holes are NPTH by default, including holes expected to receive metal screws. A plated grounding mounting hole is a separate explicit electrical footprint governed by the grounding exception below; it is not an alternate rendering of an ordinary mounting hole.

Use only these three generic NPTH configurations for locating and support features. This keeps the normal drill set small in the same way as the standard THT and via tables: | documented standard | Intended use | Finished hole | NPTH pad size | Copper clearance | Mask expansion | | locator_small_0.60 | Small plastic locating pin | 0.60 mm | 0.60 mm | 0.25 mm | 0.25 mm | | locator_standard_1.00 | Normal locating or alignment pin | 1.00 mm | 1.00 mm | 0.25 mm | 0.25 mm | | support_large_1.50 | Large nonconductive support post | 1.50 mm | 1.50 mm | 0.25 mm | 0.25 mm |

Use source_defined only when the governing manufacturer drawing requires a different diameter, an oval hole, or a non-plated slot. Record the exact source dimension and reason in the footprint checklist. Do not round a manufacturer-required locating feature to a generic size when doing so could change fit or position. A source-defined NPTH must still meet JLCPCB capability, copper-clearance, and mask-opening requirements unless its documented manufacturing exception explicitly governs.

Do not add more generic NPTH sizes merely to match a one-off source dimension. The standard metric mounting-clearance holes below are a separate approved family because they correspond to reusable fastener sizes.

For an ordinary NPTH pad: Pad type: NPTH, Mechanical (np_thru_hole). Pad number and net: blank. Hole: source-defined round or oval finished geometry. Pad size: equal to the hole geometry so no copper annulus is created. Layer set: *.Cu and *.Mask as KiCad's unplated-hole layer set. Copper clearance override: at least 0.25 mm from the finished hole edge, increased for conductive hardware or source requirements. Solder-mask expansion: 0.25 mm unless the source or fabrication profile requires another opening. Paste layers and paste clearances: none. Fabrication property: Mechanical when the NPTH occurs in an otherwise SMD footprint and that property is needed for correct KiCad DRC semantics.

Every documented NPTH must declare a stable identifier, physical role, inserted-material classification, none connection method, none electrical bond, null intended net and bond evidence, one of the approved standard names, exact center and rotation, hole and pad geometry, layer set, copper clearance, mask expansion, absence of paste, source note, and any manufacturing exception. An empty NPTH review section means the governing drawing requires no non-plated holes; it is not permission to ignore unclassified holes found in the footprint.

Place the hole center and orientation from the same datasheet datum used for the electrical pads. Include the NPTH or support feature in the physical projection used by F.Courtyard whenever it governs assembly clearance.

The following unthreaded NPTH sizes accommodate the stated metric screw with at least 0.15 mm radial clearance after the normal negative drilled-hole tolerance. They are clearance holes, not tapped holes and not plated chassis-ground connections. | Fastener | Nominal NPTH | Manufacturing note | | mounting_m2_2.40 / M2 | 2.40 mm | drilled | | mounting_m2_5_2.90 / M2.5 | 2.90 mm | drilled | | mounting_m3_3.40 / M3 | 3.40 mm | drilled | | mounting_m4_4.50 / M4 | 4.50 mm | drilled | | mounting_m5_5.50 / M5 | 5.50 mm | drilled | | mounting_m6_6.60 / M6 | 6.60 mm | exceeds the 6.30 mm drill range and is CNC-routed; confirm routing tolerance in DFM |
Use the ordinary NPTH configuration above, including 0.25 mm copper clearance and 0.25 mm solder-mask expansion. The F.Fab outline must show the finished hole boundary with 0.05 mm line width.

For a mounting-hole-only footprint, set Not in schematic. Set Exclude from position files because the hole is not a pick-and-place item. Set Exclude from bill of materials only when the associated fastener is intentionally not procured through the project BOM; otherwise represent the actual procured hardware explicitly. Leave Do not populate off, and do not exempt the footprint from the courtyard requirement. A 3D model, when present, must represent the reviewed installed hardware rather than an arbitrary screw.

The mounting-hole courtyard must represent the maximum installed screw head, washer, standoff, nut, or tool-access envelope from the selected hardware drawing, plus the normal courtyard clearance. The clearance-hole diameter alone is not a sufficient hardware courtyard. A generic hole-only footprint must be identified as such and must not be treated as a verified fastener-head keepout.

If the screw is intended to bond to chassis or board ground, create a separate explicitly plated and numbered grounding footprint. Its checklist role is bonded_mechanical, its electrical-bond classification is explicit_grounding, and it must name the intended GND, CHASSIS, or SHIELD net plus the source or system grounding rationale. Size its copper contact area for the verified washer/head, expose the required mask, assign the intended net through the symbol and schematic, and document the complete electrical and mechanical stack. Do not turn an ordinary NPTH mounting hole into a grounding feature by adding incidental copper.

Any footprint containing at least one plated or non-plated hole must document every drilled feature independently. The review checklist must record: Hole role: electrical lead, unelectrified solderable mechanical support, explicitly bonded mechanical feature, press-fit terminal, locating pin, mounting hole, or manufacturer-required via marker. Inserted material and connection method: soldered metal, press-fit metal, deliberate mechanical electrical contact, or no electrical connection. Electrical-bond classification: symbol_terminal, none, or explicit_grounding; explicit grounding also requires the intended net and source or system bond evidence. Source maximum pin envelope or source-required finished-hole dimensions. Nominal finished-hole geometry and the resulting insertion clearance. Pad type, number, shape, size, center, orientation, and full layer set. Radial annular ring or explicit no-copper NPTH construction. Mask behavior, paste exclusion, clearance inheritance or override, zone/thermal behavior, and any fabrication property. Any use of a nonstandard drill, slot, press-fit tolerance, filled/capped via process, or reduced annular ring.

Every plated drilled feature belongs in the the THT review section; it must not remain in the generic surface-pad array. Each THT item must also state a stable identifier, physical role, inserted material, connection method, electrical-bond classification, intended net, bond evidence, approved standard or source_defined, whether its pad size is exact or a minimum, the source lead geometry and maximum envelope when available, the hole-selection basis, computed insertion clearance, inherited or overridden KiCad manufacturing fields, and any source-backed exception. An empty THT review section means the governing source requires no plated drilled features.

Verify a completed THT or mixed-technology footprint by exporting and inspecting at least copper, solder mask, Excellon drill data, and a drill map. Confirm hole count, plated versus non-plated classification, slot geometry, finished-hole callouts, pad numbering, annular rings, mask openings, courtyard, and 3D alignment. A footprint with an unspecified hole or an undocumented manufacturing exception is incomplete even when KiCad parses and exports it.

A footprint may contain at most one 3D model. A footprint referenced by a concrete device record must contain exactly one reviewed model. A generic, mounting, tooling, or otherwise unassociated footprint may contain zero or one model. The reviewed model is part of the footprint identity. If another device needs a different model, it requires a separately named footprint and review checklist even when the copper, mask, paste, fabrication, silkscreen, and courtyard geometry are otherwise identical.

After creating or changing a custom pad or separate mask/paste aperture, export and inspect F.Cu, F.Mask, and F.Paste independently. Each rendered layer must contain geometry exactly when its saved pad-layer declarations require it. The Footprint Editor view alone and a combined-layer export are not sufficient verification.

Except for a dedicated polarity character governed by FP-POL-005, every footprint text object, including visible and hidden property text and user text, must use: Font: KiCad Font Width: 1.0 mm Height: 1.0 mm Thickness: 0.15 mm Horizontal justification: center Vertical justification: center For Controls panel-layout footprints, FP-CTRL-006 through FP-CTRL-008 replace these text requirements.

Assign the standard text objects to these layers: The Reference property displaying REF is on F.Silkscreen. The Value property displaying the exact footprint name is on F.Fab. The user text ${REFERENCE} is on F.Fab. For Controls panel-layout footprints, FP-CTRL-006 through FP-CTRL-008 replace these text requirements.

Place REF and the footprint-name Value text on opposite 1.27 mm grid lines centered on footprint X coordinate 0: 1. Determine the outermost rendered vertical extent of F.Courtyard and F.Silkscreen, whichever extends farther. Include graphic line widths, the pin-one dot or polarity mark, and all other permitted silkscreen geometry. 2. Include the complete 1.0 mm text height in the clearance test. The text extends 0.50 mm above and below its center. 3. Select the nearest 1.27 mm grid line, measured from footprint origin (0,0), on which the complete text box does not touch or overlap that outermost extent. Do not skip to a farther grid line when a nearer one satisfies the rule. 4. Use the larger clearance requirement of the upper and lower extents so the two text objects can remain exact mirrors. 5. Place REF above the footprint at negative Y and place the footprint-name Value text at the exact mirrored positive-Y coordinate. For Controls panel-layout footprints, FP-CTRL-006 through FP-CTRL-008 replace these text requirements.

The F.Fab ${REFERENCE} user text is not part of the external 1.27 mm placement pair; only its layer and standard text formatting are governed here. For Controls panel-layout footprints, FP-CTRL-006 through FP-CTRL-008 replace these text requirements.
Value, lower Description, and Keywords are footprint-level metadata stored locally in the .kicad_mod file.

The Value property must equal the exact footprint name without a library prefix. Do not substitute a manufacturer part number unless the footprint name itself is intentionally manufacturer-specific. Place and format the Value text according to the Footprint text rules above.

The lower Description field must concisely describe the physical package and land pattern rather than the electrical function of a particular component. Include the applicable details: Package family or manufacturer package designation Pin or terminal count Nominal or governing body dimensions Pad pitch Exposed, thermal, mechanical, or split-pad features Nonuniform mask, paste, or manufacturer-required via features Package orientation or land-pattern variant when multiple variants exist Governing manufacturer datasheet, package drawing, or land-pattern source

State whether a land pattern is manufacturer-recommended or is an approved derivation or modification. Remove stale generator text, incorrect package descriptions, and unrelated device specifications. For a genuinely one-to-one footprint, the exact manufacturer and part number may also be included.

Keywords must be concise, space-separated search terms. Include useful package aliases, pin count, body dimensions, pitch, exposed-pad terminology, mounting technology, and manufacturer package designations. Avoid duplicates, prose, electrical ratings, and device-function terms unless the footprint is intentionally one-to-one.

The lower Description and Keywords fields are local to the footprint. Editing them, or the footprint Value, does not require rebuilding the parts database. database/parts.csv remains the source of truth for part and symbol metadata and changes only when that separate metadata must change.

The upper Datasheet and Description property fields remain blank unless a deliberately one-to-one footprint requires footprint-specific component metadata. They are not substitutes for the lower footprint Description and Keywords fields.

Every footprint with two or more numbered pins must identify pin 1, including functionally non-polarized two-pin parts, except resistors. Resistor footprints must not contain a pin-one dot, pin-one chamfer, or other pin-one indication on F.Silkscreen or F.Fab.

For footprints requiring pin-one indication under FP-IND-001, unless replaced by a conventional polarity mark as described below, the F.Silkscreen pin-1 indicator must be a circle with: Radius: 0.15 mm Fill: filled Line weight: 0.0 mm Layer: F.Silkscreen

Place the circle on the outward side of pad 1. Align its center with the center of the pad width: match the pad-center Y coordinate for a left- or right-facing pad, or the pad-center X coordinate for a top- or bottom-facing pad.

The circle center must be 0.30 mm beyond the outside edge of the pad-1 copper. This provides 0.15 mm copper-to-silkscreen clearance plus the 0.15 mm circle radius. For custom pads, measure from the actual outermost copper edge.
If the specified location is ambiguous or conflicts with other copper, do not improvise; flag the footprint for manual review against its governing datasheet.
Do not use a universal anode marker. The anode is not consistently pin 1, and package conventions normally identify polarity differently.

For polarized two-terminal parts, replace the pin-1 dot with the conventional polarity mark: Diodes, Zener diodes, and LEDs: place a cathode bar or stripe at the cathode end. When that stripe would be obscured by the installed component body, retain the cathode stripe on F.Fab and use the visible F.Silkscreen K defined by FP-POL-005. Polarized capacitors: place a + at the positive/anode end.

Place each mark according to the datasheet and symbol pin mapping. Do not assume that the anode is pin 1. Do not add a redundant pin-1 dot when the conventional polarity mark already identifies the relevant numbered pin.
ICs, transistors, mechanically polarized connectors, and other parts for which anode/cathode terminology does not apply retain the normal pin-1 dot, except resistors as specified by FP-IND-001.

Every F.Silkscreen polarity character other than + or - must be one user-text object containing the character required by the datasheet and symbol mapping, with: Font: KiCad Font Width: 2.0 mm Height: 2.0 mm Thickness: 0.40 mm Weight: bold Style: upright, not italic Mirrored: no Horizontal justification: center Vertical justification: center Rotation: 0 degrees in footprint-local coordinates Layer: F.Silkscreen. The + and - polarity signs are not text objects. Draft - as one horizontal 2.0 mm line segment with 0.40 mm line width. Draft + as two orthogonal 2.0 mm line segments, one horizontal and one vertical, with 0.40 mm line width and coincident centers. Place every polarity character or sign on the outward side of the terminal it identifies and align its center with the center of the pad width: match the pad-center Y coordinate for a left- or right-facing pad, or the pad-center X coordinate for a top- or bottom-facing pad. Place the character or sign center exactly 2.0 mm beyond the outside edge of that terminal's copper. For a 2.0 mm text box or line segment extending toward the pad, this gives a nominal 1.0 mm copper-edge gap. For custom pads, measure from the actual outermost copper edge.

F.Silkscreen may contain only: The required pin-one or conventional polarity indication defined above The standardized connector keying-side indicator defined by FP-CONN-002 and FP-CONN-003 The projected package-body outline defined for F.Fab The REF autotext defined elsewhere
Do not draw component values, pad numbers, decorative graphics, manufacturer marks, or any other symbols or figures on F.Silkscreen.

Copy the projected package-body outline from F.Fab using 0.15 mm line width, but do not reproduce an F.Fab pin-one chamfer. Restore the true projected outside corner on F.Silkscreen because the separate pin-one or polarity indication identifies orientation.

When the complete outline does not intersect any F.Cu feature, draw it as one continuous, closed, unfilled rectangle, circle, or polygon. When it intersects copper, clip only the affected portions: Use separate line segments for clipped straight edges. Use separate arc segments for clipped circular or curved edges. Apply the clipping rule to all F.Cu features, including numbered, custom, and unnumbered copper pads.

The nearest outside edge of the 0.15 mm silkscreen stroke must be exactly 0.15 mm from the nearest copper edge. Because the stroke extends 0.075 mm from its centerline, a clipped line-center or arc-center endpoint must be 0.225 mm from the copper edge. Measure clearance to the rendered stroke edge, not merely to the graphic centerline.

F.Fab must contain a projected outline of the physical package body. Exclude pins, leads, terminals, pads, mounting tabs, and other metal features that extend beyond the projected outside edge of the physical body.

The package outline must be one continuous, closed, unfilled object with a 0.05 mm line width. Use the primitive that accurately represents the projected body: One unfilled rectangle for a rectangular body One unfilled circle for a circular body One closed unfilled polygon, including arc segments where necessary, for all other body geometry
Separate line segments are not permitted for the package outline. This restriction applies only to the body outline, not to internal polarity or pin-one annotations.

When the manufacturer specifies or requires PCB vias as part of the land pattern, represent every required via on F.Fab with a filled circle: Center: coincident with the manufacturer-specified via center Radius: equal to one-half of the specified via-hole diameter Fill: filled Line weight: 0.0 mm

These circles are F.Fab documentation annotations and are separate from the continuous package-body outline. They do not create drilled holes, copper, mask openings, or actual PCB vias. The required physical vias must still be implemented and verified in the board design or by another explicitly approved drilled-pad method.

Resistor footprints must not have a pin-one indication on F.Fab; preserve the unmodified projected package-body outline. For other footprints requiring orientation indication, use the following hierarchy to identify orientation on F.Fab: 1. Conventional polarity indication: For a polarized part, repeat the conventional polarity mark on F.Fab instead of adding a redundant pin-one dot. - Diodes, Zener diodes, and LEDs use a cathode stripe at the cathode end. - Polarized capacitors use a + at the positive/anode end. - An A, K, or other polarity symbol must identify the actual terminal defined by the datasheet and symbol mapping; it is not automatically placed at pin 1. - Place a stripe across the device at the datasheet-defined or industry-standard location. Use 0.05 mm line width for F.Fab polarity annotations unless the governing drawing specifies otherwise. - A polarity symbol may share the nominal F.Silkscreen pin-one-dot center only when the marked polarity terminal is pin 1. F.Cu never contains a pin-one circle. 2. Chamfer: If the package outline supports an effective pin-one chamfer, replace the applicable outside corner with a diagonal connecting points exactly 0.30 mm from the original corner along each adjacent outside edge. The chamfered outline remains one closed polygon. Do not use a chamfer when it will not fit or will not identify pin 1 effectively. 3. Replicated dot: If neither a conventional polarity indication nor an effective chamfer applies, place an exact replica of the F.Silkscreen pin-one dot on F.Fab: - Same center coordinates - Radius 0.15 mm - Filled - Line weight 0.0 mm
An F.Fab dot may be outside the package body outline. F.Fab has no copper-clearance requirement, but the corresponding F.Silkscreen mark must retain the specified copper clearance.
F.Courtyard must contain one continuous, closed, unfilled outline with 0.05 mm line width. Separate line segments are not permitted.

Use manufacturer maximum physical dimensions, including stated dimensional tolerances, permitted mold flash, burrs, and protrusions, for the physical geometry. Apply tolerances relative to the governing drawing datum and include positional tolerance where specified. Use actual designed copper-pad dimensions, not inflated manufacturer land-pattern fabrication tolerances. If a governing maximum is unavailable, record the footprint as incomplete instead of assuming the nominal dimension is the maximum. The courtyard source geometry is the union of: The projected physical package body All protruding leads, pins, terminals, and mounting features All numbered, custom, and unnumbered copper pads

Solder mask, solder paste, F.Silkscreen, F.Fab annotations, pin-one indicators, polarity marks, and text do not affect the courtyard boundary. F.Silkscreen and F.Fab geometry may cross, overlap, lie inside, or extend outside F.Courtyard.
By default, construct the tight rectangular bounding box of the complete source-geometry union. Expand each side by exactly 0.25 mm, measured from the source geometry to the F.Courtyard line center.

When the physical package body has a substantial concavity open to the exterior and the rectangular bounding box would reserve physically empty, usable PCB area, F.Courtyard may instead be one continuous, closed, concave polygon: 1. Begin with the true projected physical-body outline. 2. Union it with every protruding lead, pin, terminal, mounting feature, and copper pad. 3. Offset the combined geometry outward by exactly 0.25 mm to the F.Courtyard line center. 4. Preserve a concavity only where the offset leaves physically usable PCB area.

The concave polygon must not self-intersect or contain separate islands. A concavity must represent genuinely empty space accessible from outside the package; an F.Fab pin-one chamfer, polarity annotation, or graphical detail does not qualify. Do not preserve a concavity beneath an overhanging part of the physical package.

A manufacturer keepout or assembly-clearance requirement overrides this exception. If a concave opening is 0.50 mm wide or less, the two 0.25 mm offsets meet and the courtyard notch disappears. Fully enclosed holes or voids remain captured inside the single outer courtyard outline.

For panel-layout controls, keep the component outline, mounting geometry, origin and 3D model at their true positions. Numbered pads are wiring connection points in this elevation view. The fan-out rules below are an exception to exact pad-center placement for terminals that overlap in projection; they do not define a PCB manufacturing land pattern.

Use one pad for each terminal represented in the symbol. One terminal stays centered at its screw location. For two terminals that overlap in elevation, put their pads at equal distances to the left and right of the shared projected screw center. For three or more, put all pad centers on one circle centered there, equally spaced by 360 degrees divided by the terminal count: three at 120 degrees, four at 90 degrees, five at 72 degrees, and so on. Do not leave an extra electrical pad at the center of a fanned-out group.

Use the smallest practical common radius that leaves a small visible gap between the fanned-out pads and the screw outline, between neighboring pads, and around their labels. Account for the actual pad sizes and nearby terminals. Keep the arrangement balanced and gracefully close to the screw. Increase the radius only as needed; keep equal angular spacing.

Keep every existing symbol pin ID and its physical terminal mapping. For two pads, use the left/right arrangement. For three or more, start with one pad above the screw and distribute the rest clockwise; the whole group may rotate for clearer labeling or routing while preserving its center, radius and equal angular spacing. Follow documented terminal order where available and label terminal tiers when needed to distinguish their physical locations.

Keep the actual screw geometry visible. Do not add spokes or leader lines to fanned-out pads; their symmetric spacing implies the shared projected screw center. Record true terminal coordinates and heights where known in the footprint review data. Displaced pads are wiring targets; their positions do not change the physical outline, mounting geometry or 3D model.
For Controls panel-layout footprints, show only the Reference property. Hide the Value and all other property or user text, including duplicate reference text. Keep the metadata.
Use KiCad Font at 2.5 x 2.5 mm, 0.15 mm stroke, centered horizontally and vertically. Keep the reference horizontal on Dwgs.User with the elevation drawing.

Center the reference horizontally on the footprint drawing's vertical centerline. Place it between the topmost drawing line and the midpoint of that centerline. Move it vertically to avoid drawing lines and terminal pads; if no clear position exists, minimize overlap. Prefer fitting the whole text in this upper half where space permits. Keep the specified font size and leave the physical geometry unchanged.
Use the exact manufacturer part number or documented generic device. Check the symbol against its governing datasheet.
Show every physical electrical terminal exactly once, including unused and no-connect terminals.
Use the datasheet pin numbers, including exposed pads, separate power terminals, connector contacts, and electrical shield or mounting terminals.
Name every pin for its datasheet function. Use short, clear abbreviations: GREEN becomes GRN and ground becomes GND. Keep the physical pin mapping clear.
Give each pin its correct KiCad electrical type, such as power_in, power_out, input, output, bidirectional, passive, open_collector, or no_connect.
Use ~{NAME} for active-low pins and + or - for differential pins. Match the datasheet polarity.
Do not stack or hide pins. Every pin must be visible at its own connection point.
Use no_connect only for pins the datasheet identifies as no-connect. A usable pin that is often left unwired keeps its actual electrical type.
Non-connector pins are 100 mil (2.54 mm) long. Connector pins are 0 mm long.
For IC-style rectangular bodies, end each pin line at the body edge, with the name inside and number outside. Multi-pin J connectors use the centered zero-length pins in SYM-CONN-001.

Draw multi-pin J connectors as one vertical column of stacked 100 mil (2.54 mm) squares, one square per pin. Center a visible zero-length pin in each square. Center the whole column at the origin. Order pins from top to bottom by connector numbering or the specified functional order. Keep pin IDs and function labels legible, without overlap. Use this layout instead of IC-style side groups, ground placement, body margins and width rules. LCSC:XH-4A is the typical layout reference.
Include every unit and its correct identifier and pin assignments. Put each physical pin in one unit; show shared power pins in their assigned unit.

Use each unit's tallest required pin stack to set its grid. Count pins and blank rows using SYM-GRID-003. An odd row count uses 0, +/-100, +/-200 mil; an even row count uses +/-50, +/-150, +/-250 mil. Shorter groups follow their top or bottom anchor, not their own row-count parity. Keep horizontal connection positions on the 100 mil (2.54 mm) grid.

Place the MPN, reference designator, and Part Name on the 50 mil (1.27 mm) grid. After changing body size or position, reposition these fields relative to the new body edges using the nearest clear grid positions.

Count one row per pin, plus one blank row for each 200 mil (5.08 mm) gap between adjacent groups. Larger gaps add one blank row per extra 100 mil (2.54 mm). Count the compact stacks in each unit separately to determine its minimum body height. Spare space from a taller opposite side does not change that unit's grid alignment.
Center a rectangular pin-block body at the Symbol Editor origin (0, 0). Anchor the pin groups to the body as described below; do not vertically center each side independently.

Put dedicated device supply pins in the top-left position, starting 100 mil (2.54 mm) below the body top. Group multiple supply pins by function. Coil terminals and floating contact commons are functional pins, not automatically device supply or ground pins.
Put an enable or similar control pin 100 mil (2.54 mm) below the supply group when that connection pattern applies. Do not create an enable position when there is no such pin.

Put inputs and other left-side functions below any supply/enable group, except feedback pins covered by SYM-LAYOUT-012. Leave 200 mil (5.08 mm) between groups and 100 mil (2.54 mm) within a group. With no dedicated supply group, start the first functional group 100 mil below the body top.

Keep related pins together. Order left-side functional groups for expected wiring and the fewest likely crossings, considering high-side or low-side switching and supply or return connections. Keep dedicated supply and ground groups in their assigned positions. If expected use is unknown, preserve a clear functional order without assuming a ground connection.

Put dedicated GND, AGND, PGND and other documented device ground/return pins in the bottom-left position, with the last pin 100 mil (2.54 mm) above the body bottom. Leave at least 200 mil (5.08 mm) after the preceding group. With only supply and ground groups, keep them at the top and bottom and leave the middle empty. Do not classify floating coil or contact terminals as ground merely from their names.

Start the first right-side group 100 mil (2.54 mm) below the body top, even when there is only one group. Put the most important function first, then the remaining groups in order. Missing groups and absent unused pins never move the first group downward. Leave spare height below the last group.

Put remaining outputs on the right, 200 mil (5.08 mm) below the preceding group. Omit absent groups and do not repeat pins. If outputs are the first or only right-side group, start them at the top position.

Put low-priority or normally unused pins last on the right, 200 mil (5.08 mm) below the preceding group. If this is the only group, start it at the top position. NC meaning normally closed is a contact function, not an unused pin.
Space pins within each right-side group 2.54 mm apart.

Keep the first right-side group at the top and leave extra space below the last group. On the left, keep dedicated supply at the top and ground at the bottom; put spare space before the bottom ground group. Do not invent or split groups to fill space, or stretch a compact functional group.
For pin placement, treat feedback pins that need a resistor divider or another non-GND connection as outputs and place them in the right-side output group. Keep their datasheet electrical pin type.

The left side has top supply, middle functional/input and bottom ground positions, not three mandatory groups. Use only the groups the part actually has; do not invent or split groups to fill all positions. A coil terminal pair stays together unless the documented function requires otherwise. Order floating functional groups using SYM-LAYOUT-005.

Within each functional group, prefer supply-connected pins toward the top and return or pull-down pins toward the bottom. Place pins likely to share a connection near one another across adjacent groups while preserving group separation. Base the order on documented function and expected use, not pin names alone; do not assume an electrical connection from placement.

For control devices, distinguish the two ends of a contact with short names such as AUX_NO_1 and AUX_NO_2. The suffix identifies the end of one contact, not another contact. Use position suffixes such as A1_TOP and A1_BOT for duplicate access terminals. Keep the factory terminal numbers and existing documented pin-ID qualifiers unchanged.

For control devices, keep both ends of each contact adjacent on the same side, 100 mil (2.54 mm) apart. Keep duplicate access points to the same internal node adjacent too. Keep the coil terminals in one group; give each auxiliary contact its own group, with 200 mil (5.08 mm) between groups. Contact grouping takes priority over the IC-style input/output layout. Functional groups may use either side to keep the symbol clear, for example LOW at left and HIGH at right; keep each contact pair intact. Main power poles may keep line terminals on the left and matching load terminals on the right to show power flow.

A control unit may have all pins on the left when it has no distinct outputs. Do not move a contact end to the right just to fill that side. An empty side needs no group or extra body space. Keep the actual electrical pin types, centered body, pin grid and field placement rules. Multi-pin J connectors still use SYM-CONN-001.

Size each unit from its own taller compact pin stack, including blank group-separation rows. Add 100 mil (2.54 mm) at each end and center the body at the origin. Do not enlarge a short unit to match another unit. Position the placed fields relative to that unit's body.
After placing the pin names, make the rectangle as narrow as possible without overlapping names on opposite sides.
Keep the reference designator and schematic value visible, correct, and legible. Keep text clear of pins, other text, and the body outline.

For an IC, center the exact MPN horizontally above the rectangle. Use the nearest 1.27 mm grid position where the whole text is outside the body and does not touch its top line. If Value already displays the MPN, do not display it twice.
Center the reference designator above the MPN at the next 1.27 mm grid position that keeps the two texts from touching.

Center Part Name below the rectangle. Use the nearest 1.27 mm grid position where the whole text is outside the body and does not touch its bottom line. Check placed schematic fields too: automatic placement must not move Part Name above the body or connector labels to the side.
Describe the function in as few words as possible, preferably two or three main words. Examples: Adjustable Voltage Regulator, USB Controller, Voltage Comparator.
Arrange Part Name in two or three lines to suit its length, with one or two words per line.
Keep Value, MPN, Description, Keywords, Datasheet, footprint filters, and other device properties accurate. Hide metadata fields except the visible schematic labels defined by these rules.
Include the Part Name metadata field. It is required for ICs and other parts drawn as rectangular pin blocks. Its default is [part name]. Leave it blank when it does not apply.
Keep symbol definitions limited to device information. Put review notes, change history, uncertainties, and conversation commentary in review documents, not symbol properties.
Use the exact reviewed footprint for a concrete device. Match symbol pin numbers to footprint pad numbers without renumbering.
Open the symbol in KiCad and check pin order, labels, electrical types, body geometry, fields, units, and readability at normal editing scale.

For DIN-mounted Controls, put the footprint origin at the center of the mounting width on the rail centerline. Use the same X/Y origin in the STEP model. Z=0 is the front face of the backplate, where the rear of the rail rests. The body envelope does not determine the rail centerline.

Use a horizontal rail along model X, panel up along model +Y, and the component front toward +Z. The standard rail is 35 x 7.5 mm, with its lips at Z=7.5 mm. Place each device at its installed height using its actual groove or clip geometry. Do not add 7.5 mm blindly to the back of every device. A 15 mm rail needs a separately verified placement.

Save the installed orientation and translation in a clearly named derived STEP. Link that STEP with model offset 0,0,0; rotation 0,0,0; and scale 1,1,1. Move footprint graphics, text and pads together when changing its X/Y origin. Preserve terminal IDs and physical dimensions. The rail itself may use a cardinal rotation to select its length direction.

Keep the manufacturer STEP unchanged. Record the source, rigid transform, mounting reference and rail profile for each derived model. Check model dimensions, terminal alignment and the nominal rail fit. Keep source clip states; report overlaps or missing mounting details instead of trimming geometry or claiming an unverified fit.

An overload, auxiliary block, interlock, suppressor or busbar that mounts to a contactor uses its host mating datum. Do not independently center it on the DIN rail. Panel-mounted variants retain their panel mounting datum.

For DIN rail and wire duct, put (0,0,0) at the center of the back left edge with the part running horizontally along +X. Center the cross-section across model Y; +Z points toward the enclosure front and the rear mounting face is Z=0. This replaces the centered device datum in FP-DIN-001 for rail and duct only. Keep reference text centered over the physical drawing. Use length-specific PartIDs while retaining the manufacturer stock MPN. When changing a placed footprint origin, preserve its physical position, angle, text and geometry.
